findings.reason: The Definition assigns |D_s| to any h with integrable Fourier transform, then asserts absolute convergence. Integrability of hat(h) alone does not ensure |sigma|·hat(h)(sigma) is integrable, and the stated Fourier-transform domain is C_c^infty. Make the filter input class explicit so the transform is defined by the stated convention and the displayed integral converges absolutely; existing |D_s| uses are on Rf for compactly supported smooth f.

Step 2.1 applies the Riemann–Fubini supplier, whose statement is real-valued, directly to a complex integrand. The proof also uses hat(Rf) without establishing Rf is in the Definition's C_c^infty Fourier-transform domain. Locally establish smoothness and compact support of the line data, then apply Fubini separately to real and imaginary parts.
The finite output is denoted f_tilde_h, but h is never defined; detector spacing Delta s = 1 is not identified with h. Define h or use an un-subscripted output notation consistently.
